title: Not only human but also God
english: The one who appeared on earth and lived among human beings is not only a human being but also God, just as Jeremiah the prophet also says: “This is our God; no other will be reckoned beside him” (Jeremiah).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius opens a fragment by stating the claim he will defend: the one who appeared on earth is not only human but also God, as Jeremiah the prophet says.

title: The divine-human shared life with humans
english: He found out the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel whom he loved (Baruch 3:36-38, appended to Jeremiah). After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings. And when did he live among human beings, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin, shared infancy, grew up together with them, ate and drank with them, and shared all the rest of human life?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius continues the quotation from Jeremiah, then presses its claim that this divine figure lived among human beings by asking when that shared life happened.

title: Providence for the whole catholic Church
english: For if, he says, prayers must be made for the catholic Church that is from the ends of the world, then far more must providence be displayed for all of it, and one must care and be anxious for all of them equally.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is arguing that if prayers must be made for the catholic Church spread across the world, then all the more must providential care be shown for the whole Church.
